filing_type: News pilot — official Tadawul issuer announcements plus named third-party press coverage
notes:
First application of the two-tier news sourcing policy agreed for this project: Tier 1 (official_announcement) is Tadawul's own Announcements tab on the same company-profile page already used for the market/ownership manifest (retrieved 2026-09-11/12) -- same trust level as a financial disclosure, since it is the exchange's own record of the issuer's own filing. Tier 2 (press_coverage) is third-party journalism from named, identifiable outlets only, each carrying its own source name, URL and date in metadata so it can never be displayed as an engine-verified fact -- per the agreed rule, every press item must show 'per [outlet]' to the reader, not be presented as a bare number.

Tier 2 sourcing note on attribution certainty: the sukuk-pricing item below was retrieved from a tradingview.com URL whose own identifier pattern ('reuters.com,2026-09-04:newsml_...') is TradingView's standard tag for syndicated Reuters wire content, but the fetched page itself credited 'Zawya/Refinitiv' in its byline area. Since the two attributions could not be independently reconciled from the fetched content alone, this manifest cites the verifiable publisher of the page actually retrieved (TradingView, carrying a Reuters-tagged wire story) rather than asserting 'Reuters' outright -- an example of not resolving a sourcing ambiguity by picking the more prestigious-sounding name.

No update schedule is wired for this manifest yet -- it is a one-time pilot fill, not a running monitor. Per the agreed cadence policy, news should refresh daily (unlike weekly for disclosures/financials) once an automated connector exists; none exists yet, this was a manual pull.

disclosures.title: Al Rajhi Bank prices a $600mln Tier 2 social sukuk
disclosures.body_text: Third-party press coverage (not an engine-verified fact -- attribute to the named publisher when displayed): Al Rajhi Bank priced a USD 600 million Tier 2 social sukuk at a profit rate of 6.232%, 10.5-year maturity with a 5.25-year non-call period, issued at par and listed on the London Stock Exchange's International Securities Market. Final order books exceeded USD 1.25 billion (peaking above USD 1.85 billion during bookbuilding).
